title: Domain Attribute Validation, Departure from RFC6265bis
body:
Greetings folks 👋 

Ran into this error path today, initially I thought it was a bug / oversight in the chromium implementation but as I dug into it more it seems like an explicit decision made by the authors of this specification.

[RFC 6265bis Section 4.1.2.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis-03#section-4.1.2.3) states,

> (Note that a leading %x2E ("."), if present, is ignored even though that character is not permitted...

It looks like this part of the spec is explicitly ignored in web-platform-test suites, and the leading `.` is treated an an error path:

- https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/4587eeb11970eb2a66f96513622fcb64556f08d9/cookie-store/cookieStore_delete_arguments.https.any.js#L29-L32
- https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/cookie-store/cookieStore_set_arguments.https.any.js#L109-L117

That leads me to believe it was a conscious decision. 

I can not find any discussions on why that decision was made. My gut reaction is that this validation _should not_ take place and depart from the specification. Happy to provide a more compelling argument if yall are willing to entertain it, but first wanted to know the history behind the decision.
